MAJOR: `_git` now raises on any non-zero rc, making the `or "origin/develop"` fallback dead code; if `git merge-base develop HEAD` fails (detached/single-branch CI, no local `develop`) the whole gate crashes instead of degrading.

AC states `JSONDecodeError` propagates; `_load` wraps it in `RuntimeError`, so any caller/handler keyed on `JSONDecodeError` (or on the raw cause contract) never observes it — conform or amend the AC.
`transitions()` prints a plain-text line to stderr, violating the documented "one JSON line on stderr" contract and breaking machine consumers of the report.

`_load` reads the working-tree file rather than the committed blob (`git show HEAD:<path>`/`base:<path>`), so uncommitted local edits or partial checkouts can count a transition that is not actually committed — the AC explicitly claims a *committed* transition is detected.
The AC's "the gate prints the real completion count" is not evidenced anywhere in the diff (only a skipped-path warning was added); the count-emitting change must be shown or verified.
MINOR: `@functools.lru_cache` on `_repo_root()` never invalidates; tests only pass by monkeypatching the symbol, so the real cached code path is untested and the test/impl coupling is brittle.
`allow_fail=True` on `git show` + `prev = {}` conflates "path absent at base" with "bad base/sha/other git error", silently inflating the transition count with no distinguishing log.
`store-registry.json` gains a test-fixture glob (`BI-TEST-*.json`) in production config: registry pollution, root-unscoped, and unrelated to the stated AC.
Skipped paths are only announced on stderr when >0 and are not carried as a structured field in the JSON report, so the visibility is not machine-queryable.
NIT: The `delivery-completeness:` error prefix is duplicated across every raise; extract a single helper/prefix constant.
`test_transitions_uses_repo_root` only exercises the happy path; no test that a malformed changed item aborts `transitions()` rather than being skipped.
New `import pytest` assumes pytest is the runner for this test file; confirm the repo's test-framework invocation matches.
SUMMARY: Direction is right: repo-root resolution, path-escape guard, and fail-closed loading are genuine integrity improvements over silently joining to `product-forge/ROOT`.

Top risks: a new hard-failure mode where a fallback previously existed, a broken stderr JSON contract, and reading the worktree instead of the committed blob, which weakens the "committed transition" guarantee.
Recommend landing only after the `_git` fallback, stderr contract, and committed-vs-worktree read are resolved.
